_purpose: Standing config for COT Supplier Dashboard rescans. Load this FIRST in any new session before rescanning suppliers/delivery platforms/SumUp/Kassenbuch, instead of reconstructing folder IDs and logic from memory text or old chats.

github.push_method: PAT via curl (GET sha, then PUT with base64 content). Always fetch current sha first to avoid overwrite conflicts. Use GitHub API, not raw.githubusercontent.com, for pre-edit reads (CDN can be stale).
github.note: PAT is not persisted between sessions (fresh container each time) - must be re-supplied by Munjal when pushing is needed.

optional_fields: summary (for bulk-basket suppliers like Metro/Kupfer where full lineItems aren't worth extracting)
rescan_procedure: 1. Fetch current manifest.json from repo to get each supplier's latestInvoiceDate
2. For each supplier folder, Google Drive:search_files with parentId + modifiedTime > latestInvoiceDate (or a safe buffer before it)
3. Dedupe against existing invoiceNo list in that supplier's dataFile (fetch from repo) - many re-uploads/duplicate filenames of the same invoice appear
4. Parse contentSnippet OCR text for new invoices only
5. Batch all new invoices across all suppliers, append to respective JSON files, recompute manifest totals in ONE pass
6. Push all changed files in one batch at the end, not one push per supplier

Wolt.unit: period (weekly-ish, ~5 day cycles, 3 files per period: merchant invoice/fee, payout report, sales report)

Uber Eats.unit: week (Mon-Sun), source = weekly Aktivitätsübersicht PDF + official quarterly-ish fee invoice PDFs (0000029 etc, link via officialInvoiceNo)
Uber Eats.authoritative_monthly_source: Uber's own 'sales-over-time' CSV export (user uploads periodically) - use this for monthly gross totals instead of summing weekly PDFs when available, it's ground truth and cheaper to process

This is calendar-month aligned (unlike weekly invoices which cross month boundaries) - prefer this for monthly totals, replace weekly-derived monthly figures when available.

Rows with Konto='chutneyontop@gmail.com' and Beschreibung like 'Wolt 7% lieferung'/'Lieferando 7%'/'Uber 19%' are the AGENDA-workflow delivery-platform revenue pass-through bookings entered directly into SumUp (per AGENDA_Kassenbuch_Import_Referenz.md logic) - do not double-count against the separate Wolt/UberEats/Lieferando JSON files, these are the same money booked a second way for cash-register purposes.

recipe_costing_yield_rules.chicken: 1kg raw chicken shrinks to approx. 700g usable/cooked weight before use (70% yield) - use this when calculating chicken portion costs. NOTE: existing recipes.json entries for chicken dishes (Butter Chicken, CTM etc) were built using an older 60% yield assumption (250g raw -> 150g cooked) - these need recalculation to the corrected 70% yield if/when recipes.json is next touched.
recipe_costing_yield_rules.paneer: 10L milk yields approx. 1kg house-made paneer. Milk ~€1.05/L -> paneer house cost ~€10.50/kg.

known_data_quirks: Google Drive:read_file_content applies markdown-style backslash-escaping to underscores/brackets/hashes in returned text, which corrupts JSON/CSV when copy-pasted for reconstruction. Always prefer Google Drive:download_file_content (raw base64) for any file whose exact byte content matters (CSVs, JSONs to be parsed). Even download_file_content occasionally introduces a stray trailing brace if hand-transcribed through the chat - decode programmatically (base64.b64decode) rather than retyping content.
Duplicate re-uploads: the same invoice sometimes appears as multiple Drive files with near-identical or '(1)' suffixed names - dedupe by invoiceNo, not by filename or fileId.
Wolt periods sometimes have only 1-2 of the 3 expected documents (merchant invoice/payout report/sales report) - note incompleteness in driveFileIds rather than fabricating missing figures.

manifest.revenueByPlatform is a CUMULATIVE snapshot from a specific past reconciliation (dated 27.07.2026 as of Aug 2026) - it does NOT auto-update from the weekly wolt.json/uber_eats.json/lieferando.json files. These are two separate data views kept intentionally distinct in the dashboard UI.
